content: CHHIP stands for Conventional or Hypofractionated High Dose Intensity Modulated Radiotherapy for Prostate Cancer. It is a treatment protocol currently being evaluated in clinical trials for the management of prostate cancer using external beam radiotherapy. The primary arm of the protocol involves delivering a total dose of 74 Gy to the prostate. Additional optional target volumes, such as the seminal vesicles and lymph nodes, may receive prescribed doses of 71 Gy and 59 Gy, respectively. For each target, at least 95% of the prescribed dose must be delivered to at least 99% of the target volume. Additionally, the dose to the hottest 1% of the target volume must be recorded. Dose constraints are applied to minimize radiation exposure to healthy tissues. For the rectum: No more than 68% of the dose (50 Gy) should be delivered to 60% of the rectum. No more than 81% of the dose (60 Gy) should be delivered to 50% of the rectum. No more than 88% of the dose (65 Gy) should be delivered to 30% of the rectum. No more than 95% of the dose (70 Gy) should be delivered to 15% of the rectum. No more than 100% of the dose (74 Gy) should be delivered to 5% of the rectum. For the femoral heads: No more than 50% of the volume should receive more than 68% of the dose (50 Gy). For the bladder: No more than 68% of the dose (50 Gy) should be delivered to 50% of the bladder volume. No more than 81% of the dose (60 Gy) should be delivered to 25% of the bladder volume. No more than 100% of the dose (74 Gy) should be delivered to 5% of the bladder volume. For the bowel: No more than 68% of the dose (50 Gy) should be delivered to 17 cc of the bowel. For additional targets: No more than 68% of the dose (50 Gy) should be delivered to 50% of the urethral bulb. No more than 81% of the dose (60 Gy) should be delivered to 10% of the urethral bulb. No more than 41% of the dose (30 Gy) should be delivered to 80% of the rectum. No more than 54% of the dose (40 Gy) should be delivered to 70% of the rectum. The protocol includes three arms to compare conventional fractionation (2 Gy per fraction) with hypofractionated regimens (3 Gy per fraction). The control group receives the standard 74 Gy in 37 fractions. The second arm delivers 60 Gy in 20 fractions, while the third arm delivers 57 Gy in 19 fractions. Dose constraints for the hypofractionated arms are scaled equivalents of those used in the 74 Gy arm. The trial is being led and coordinated by Professor David Dearnaley at the Institute of Cancer Research in Surrey. The goal is to recruit over 2,162 patients. As of May 2007, 671 patients had been enrolled, representing 30% of the target accrual. The trial is scheduled to conclude in 2015.
